summary: Verified partial optimization: the JIT serialized freshly generated source IR twice, and MlirCompiler.compile now reuses the retained text for the required parse copy. Cold cache keys and source/compiled IR hashes were unchanged. The isolated cold observations are not evidence of an end-to-end speedup and this narrow reduction does not resolve the broad original compile-time request.

tests.what_was_measured: Baseline cold RMSNorm 16x4096 bf16 compile and GPU execution against a float32 Torch RMSNorm reference; retained raw stage timing, cache path, cache-key hash, IR hashes and maximum absolute error.
Changed cold RMSNorm 16x4096 bf16 compile and the same independent GPU numerical reference, in a distinct empty cache.

Baseline cold gfx950 GEMM 1024x1024x1024 bf16-to-fp32 compile and GPU execution against torch float32 matmul; retained raw stage timing, cache path, cache-key hash, IR hashes and maximum absolute error.
Changed cold gfx950 GEMM in a distinct empty cache against the same independent Torch reference.
Failing-before regression on the recorded base: MlirCompiler.compile did not accept retained source IR and therefore could not avoid the second serialization.
Passing-after regression plus 19 cache identity/completeness tests.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed both kernels. RMSNorm max_abs_error=0.0009765625; GEMM max_abs_error=0.4954681396484375 within the maintained test configuration tolerance.
remaining_limitations: This is a Python JIT orchestration change, so no native C++ rebuild was required.

The exact external RMSNorm snapshot linked by the issue no longer imports against this checkout because it references removed flydsl.expr.vector APIs; measurements use the maintained in-tree RMSNorm and GEMM implementations instead.
The reported MI355 was unavailable; validation used the assigned MI350X with the same gfx950 target family.

Cold wall-clock timings are single isolated observations and include host/runtime noise. The correctness and identity hashes, rather than their small timing delta, establish unchanged output and compilation identity.
A direct attempt to remove the required parse copy caused an MLIR duplicate-attribute assertion; only the redundant second serialization was removed.
